system:
You are a cost estimation assistant for software delivery projects. Produce a realistic, well-reasoned cost estimate from the backlog and rate card provided, plus a short list of concrete cost-reduction recommendations (e.g. descoping a low-priority item, reducing a role's allocated hours, deferring non-labour spend) each with an estimated dollar saving.

Hard constraints on labourLines:
- Use ONLY the roles listed in the rate card, spelled exactly as given. Never invent a role the project does not staff, and never split or merge the listed roles.
- Use the exact hourlyRate given for each role. Do not substitute your own market rate.
- cost must equal hours x hourlyRate for every line.
- Each role's headcount is the full-time-equivalent people available in it. Keep the hours you allocate to a role proportionate to that capacity, and say so in your assumptions if a role is staffed too thinly for the backlog it has to absorb.
- Omit a role entirely rather than padding it with token hours.

Always call the submit_cost_estimate tool with your answer.

messages.content:
Project: Customer Portal (client: Northwind Ltd)
Currency: USD

Project team and rate card (these are the only roles staffed on this project):
- Backend Developer: 98.33 USD/hour, 1.5 FTE available
- Frontend Developer: 90 USD/hour, 1.0 FTE available
- QA Engineer: 70 USD/hour, 0.6 FTE available
- DevOps Engineer: 110 USD/hour, 0.4 FTE available

Backlog (24 not-yet-done tasks):
- [PW-1] Set up CI pipeline and staging environment (priority: High, points: 5)
  Build, test and deploy pipeline with a staging slot; required before any feature work ships.
- [PW-2] Design system and component library (priority: Medium, points: unestimated)
  Shared Angular component library: buttons, forms, tables, dialogs, theming tokens.
- [PW-3] User registration and login (priority: Urgent, points: 8)
  Email/password registration, login, refresh tokens, password reset over email.
- [PW-4] Role-based access control (priority: High, points: unestimated)
  Per-project roles and a permission matrix enforced in the API and the UI.
- [PW-5] Customer account dashboard (priority: High, points: 8)
  Landing view after login: open orders, recent invoices, account health.
- [PW-6] Invoice list and detail view (priority: Medium, points: unestimated)
  Paged invoice list with filters, plus a detail view with downloadable PDF.
- [PW-7] Payment provider integration (priority: Urgent, points: 13)
  Integrate Stripe for card payments including webhooks and reconciliation.
- [PW-8] Legacy data migration (priority: High, points: unestimated)
  Migrate 400k customer records and 2M invoice lines from the legacy Oracle schema.
- [PW-9] GDPR data export and deletion (priority: High, points: 8)
  Self-service export of personal data and a verified deletion workflow.
- [PW-10] Audit log (priority: Medium, points: unestimated)
  Append-only audit trail for account, payment and permission changes.
- [PW-11] Email notification service (priority: Medium, points: 5)
  Transactional email with templating, retry and bounce handling.
- [PW-12] Support ticket submission (priority: Low, points: unestimated)
  Customers raise tickets from the portal; tickets sync to the existing helpdesk.
- [PW-13] Search across invoices and orders (priority: Medium, points: 8)
  Full-text search with filters over invoices and orders.
- [PW-14] Multi-currency support (priority: Medium, points: unestimated)
  Display and settle invoices in EUR, USD and PLN with daily FX rates.
- [PW-15] Accessibility pass to WCAG 2.2 AA (priority: Medium, points: 8)
  Keyboard navigation, contrast, screen-reader labels across all screens.
- [PW-16] Performance hardening of invoice list (priority: Medium, points: unestimated)
  Invoice list must render under 1.5s at p95 for accounts with 10k+ invoices.
- [PW-17] Two-factor authentication (priority: High, points: 8)
  TOTP-based second factor, enrolment and recovery codes.
- [PW-18] Admin back-office for support staff (priority: Low, points: unestimated)
  Internal screens for support agents to inspect and correct customer data.
- [PW-19] Usage analytics and reporting (priority: Low, points: 8)
  Per-account usage dashboards with CSV export for finance.
- [PW-20] Mobile responsive layout (priority: Medium, points: unestimated)
  All customer-facing screens usable on phones from 360px width.
- [PW-21] Rate limiting and abuse protection (priority: Medium, points: 5)
  Per-IP and per-account throttling on authentication and export endpoints.
- [PW-22] Observability: tracing and dashboards (priority: Medium, points: unestimated)
  Distributed tracing, error dashboards and alerting on the payment path.
- [PW-23] Contract tests against the helpdesk API (priority: Low, points: 5)
  Consumer-driven contract tests so helpdesk changes cannot break the portal silently.
- [PW-24] Decommission the legacy portal (priority: Low, points: unestimated)
  Redirect old URLs, archive the legacy app and shut down its infrastructure.

No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project — note that explicitly as an assumption rather than inventing figures.
